sections.h2: What moves a Hamilton Township, Mercer County, sale along fastest?
sections.html:
Timing comes down to a Certificate of Approval from the township's housing inspectors, a settled tax balance and a deed recorded in Trenton. This page covers the Hamilton beside Trenton, which is a separate place from the Atlantic County township with the same name.

It is the most populous municipality in Mercer County, with a Census Bureau estimate of 94,157 residents for July 1, 2025. Owners live in 71.6 percent of homes, and the typical owner-occupied value is $335,500. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands removes the loan approval and repair requests that often stretch a conventional timeline.

sections.h2: How is Hamilton Township laid out for a seller?
sections.html:
Hamilton covers 39.44 square miles and is the largest suburb of Trenton, the state capital, which lies to its west. It has no true downtown. Separate communities act as commercial centers instead: Mercerville (13,447 residents in 2020), Hamilton Square (12,679), White Horse (9,791), Yardville (6,965) and Groveville (3,106).

Incorporation came on April 11, 1842, and the name comes from Hamilton Square. Open space is a draw: Veterans Park fills 350 acres inside the township, Mercer County Park's 2,500 acres adjoin it to the north, and Grounds For Sculpture occupies 42 acres. Retirement communities and assisted-living facilities have gone up near Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital Hamilton, and new restaurants, banks and stores have opened along Route 33.

  • Mercerville and Hamilton Square: the two most populous census-designated places.
  • White Horse: in the southern part of the township, where the 1733 Isaac Pearson House stands.
  • Groveville: the smallest of the five census-designated places.

The Isaac Watson House of 1708, the oldest house in Mercer County, stands near White Horse. The Postal Service officially treats many Hamilton addresses as Trenton, so state the township name in your advertising.

sections.html:

The state's 2025 general rate for the township is 3.708 per $100, with an effective rate of 2.434. Average sales ran about $187,000 above the average assessment, so recent nearby closings are a better guide to price than older averages.

sections.h2: What approval does Hamilton Township require before occupancy changes?
sections.html:
Before any change in occupancy of a house or apartment, the Office of Housing Inspection and Landlord Compliance has to issue a Certificate of Approval stating that the building and premises meet township ordinances. The township names life safety as the first priority of the inspection.

Applications go through the Change of Occupancy Application Portal or on paper to the office. A Change of Occupancy Checklist is published, and reading it before the inspector arrives is the cheapest way to avoid a second visit. The township does not inspect houses for lead on request, so a seller who wants a lead test must hire a private inspector.

  • Apply once you have a signed contract so the approval is fresh at closing.
  • Check smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, since state rules require a certificate valid for six months on one-family and two-family sales.
  • Fix visible safety problems, such as loose rails and missing detectors, before the appointment.

The construction office keeps a house's blueprints for 10 years, so ask for plans if you need to show a buyer what was built. The Land Use Office can confirm a parcel's zoning designation.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Hamilton Township?
sections.html:
The Mercer County Board of Taxation, at 640 South Broad Street in Trenton, certifies assessments and hears appeals. Regular appeals are due April 1, appeals over added or omitted assessments are due December 1, and in-person filing runs from 8:30 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. Postcards with the new assessment go out at the end of January, so read yours before deciding to file.

The county's Property Information Portal shows property record cards, sales, deeds and tax information, which helps you locate comparable sales near your street before you decide whether to file. Request a written tax payoff from the township collector before closing.

sections.h2: What will a Hamilton Township seller pay, and where does the deed go?
sections.html:
The state's Realty Transfer Fee falls on the seller at recording. For a price above $350,000 the rate starts at $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, and the schedule steps up in higher brackets, so a $450,000 sale lands near $3,695. The county clerk adds that deeds above $1,000,000 recorded since July 10, 2025 carry a revised fee under a new state law.

Real estate transfers are recorded at the Mercer County Clerk's Office, 209 South Broad Street in Trenton, where title searchers and the public can view a property's history in the records room or online. Resident sellers sign the GIT/REP-3 residency certification. Sellers who live elsewhere prepay Gross Income Tax of 2 percent of the price or more.

  • State transfer fee, set by the rate table.
  • Mortgage and lien payoffs.
  • The seller's share of the quarter's property tax.
  • Certificate and inspection fees set by the township.

sections.h2: What if I am selling a Hamilton Township rental?
sections.html:
About 28 percent of occupied homes in Hamilton are rented, and typical rent is $1,634. The same housing inspection office that approves owner sales handles any change of occupancy in a house, dwelling unit or apartment, so a rental turning over to a new tenant or a new owner passes through it as well.

Gather leases, move-out dates and repair records before you apply. A buyer who plans to rent the house will need approval for the next tenancy as well, so a clean inspection record helps the sale.

sections.h2: How do highways, trains and schools shape Hamilton Township demand?
sections.html:
Hamilton is the only New Jersey municipality hosting Interstate 95 along with both of its auxiliary routes, I-195 and I-295, plus U.S. Routes 130 and 206 and Routes 29, 33 and 156. The township lies about 65 miles from New York City and 35 miles from Philadelphia. The Hamilton station on Sloan Avenue, off I-295 Exit 65B, serves NJ Transit's Northeast Corridor and logged 3,635 average weekday boardings in 2025, the eighth-highest in the state.

The Hamilton Township School District runs 23 schools, including three high schools named Nottingham (North), Hamilton West and Steinert (East), and reported 11,816 students in the 2021 to 2022 school year. Water comes from Aqua New Jersey or Trenton Water Works, so confirm which utility serves the house.

faqs.q: Which approval must a seller get in Hamilton Township, Mercer County?
faqs.a: A Certificate of Approval from the Office of Housing Inspection and Landlord Compliance, required before a change of occupancy. Apply through the township portal or with the office's paper forms.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed in Hamilton Township?
faqs.a: With the Mercer County Board of Taxation at 640 South Broad Street in Trenton by April 1. Appeals over added or omitted assessments are due December 1.

faqs.q: Will the township test my house for lead before a sale?
faqs.a: No, it does not test houses for lead on request. A seller who wants a test has to hire a private inspector.

faqs.q: Which office records a Hamilton Township deed?
faqs.a: The Mercer County Clerk's Office at 209 South Broad Street in Trenton. Deeds above $1,000,000 recorded since July 10, 2025 carry a revised fee under the new state law.

faqs.q: Why do some Hamilton addresses say Trenton?
faqs.a: The Postal Service officially treats many Hamilton addresses as Trenton even though the house is in Hamilton Township. Name the township in your listing so buyers can find the right tax and school information.
